## Section A — field origins

One tree per operation. Names are the **C# records and properties** the operation folder will hold
(`ShapeKey`), because this section is read by whoever writes
`Presentation/Endpoints/<Resource>/<Operation>/`; the wire keys stay snake_case in `openapi.yaml`
and the mapping is mechanical. Types are the **contract's**, not C#'s. `?` marks the 3.1 union
`type: [x, "null"]`. `conf` is **high** for a typed column, **med** for an acceptance criterion or a
named convention, **low** for an inference.

The origin sits on the row it belongs to and wraps under itself. Nothing is pushed into a footnote,
so a reviewer reads a claim and its source without moving their eyes off the line.

A `$ref`'d schema is expanded once, under the first operation that carries it.

**One C# record per operation folder, even when two serialise identically** (`CLAUDE.md` §API). So
`LoadStatementResponse` and `MigrateHistoryResponse` are two records over one `ImportRunResult`
schema, and `GetImportRunResponse` and `UndoImportRunResponse` are two over one `ImportRunReport`.
The `$ref` keeps the document from drifting against itself; the separate records keep one
operation's change from reshaping another endpoint.

### `inspectFile` — `POST /api/v1/mapping-profiles/inspect`

```text
request  InspectFileRequest                                (multipart/form-data)
└─ File                   binary           med  ← the file, read and dropped. ADR-0001 — it is never stored. No
                                                  maxLength: PRD §8's file-size ceiling is open, and data-model.md
                                                  decision 10 says the column bounds do not close it

response 200  FileInspectionResponse
├─ ShapeKey               string(1000)     high ← mapping_profiles.shape_key — the normalised header row
│                                                 (ADR-0009, decision 2): column names trimmed and lowercased,
│                                                 trailing empty columns dropped, joined with a pipe, in the
│                                                 file's own order. Readable, not hashed
├─ MappingProfileId       uuid?            high ← mapping_profiles.id. null means this shape is new and its rules
│                                                 are not confirmed yet
└─ SourceCategories[]     string(200)[]    med  ← PRD AC-01 — the file's own categories, read from the file and
                                                  never stored on their own. The bound is copied from
                                                  mapping_profile_rules.source_category VARCHAR(200)
```

### `confirmMappingProfile` — `POST /api/v1/mapping-profiles`

```text
request  ConfirmMappingProfileRequest
├─ ShapeKey               string(1000)     high ← mapping_profiles.shape_key. Passed back from inspectFile
│                                                 unchanged — settled at this gate in run 1. The confirm step
│                                                 carries no file (ADR-0001)
└─ Rules[]                MappingRule[]    high ← mapping_profile_rules, one row per rule. An empty list is legal:
                                                  a category the owner leaves without a rule has its rows set
                                                  aside (AC-01, AC-08)
   ├─ SourceCategory      string(200)      high ← mapping_profile_rules.source_category — the file's own category
   │                                              text, unique within one profile
   ├─ Target              enum(2)          high ← mapping_profile_rules.target VARCHAR(30) — Category or
   │                                              TransferBetweenOwnAccounts. Two values, not three (decision 1):
   │                                              a transaction names exactly one category and there is no default
   │                                              one
   └─ TargetCategoryId    uuid?            high ← mapping_profile_rules.target_category_id, NULL, FK to
                                                  categories(id). Set exactly when Target is Category — an
                                                  invariant refused in the entity, never a database CHECK
                                                  (decision 12)

response 201 | 200  MappingProfileResponse                 (201 a new shape · 200 its rules replaced)
├─ Id                     uuid             high ← mapping_profiles.id — UUID v7 minted in the Application layer
│                                                 (core-ledger ADR-0005)
├─ ShapeKey               string(1000)     high ← mapping_profiles.shape_key
├─ Rules[]                MappingRule[]    high ← the same MappingRule as the request above. AC-04 holds because
│                                                 no recorded movement points at a rule, so replacing these
│                                                 changes nothing already recorded
└─ CreatedAt              date-time        high ← mapping_profiles.created_at
```

### `loadStatement` — `POST /api/v1/import-runs/statement`

```text
request  LoadStatementRequest                              (multipart/form-data)
├─ File                   binary           med  ← the file (ADR-0001). The multipart part's filename is what lands
│                                                 in import_runs.file_name, stored and shown as plain text and
│                                                 never interpreted (PRD §6.1)
└─ AccountId              uuid             high ← import_runs.account_id, PRD AC-05. The owner names the account
                                                  the file covers; a statement covers one account, so no column in
                                                  the file is read for it (sad.md §6)

response 200  LoadStatementResponse                        (schema ImportRunResult)
├─ ImportRunId            uuid             high ← import_runs.id — UUID v7, so a run id also orders runs by when
│                                                 they happened
├─ Kind                   enum(2)          high ← import_runs.kind VARCHAR(20) — Statement or HistoryMigration,
│                                                 the two entry points of ADR-0005
├─ Status                 enum(2)          high ← import_runs.status VARCHAR(20) — Completed or Undone. No Failed:
│                                                 ADR-0004 commits the whole run at once, so a load that fails
│                                                 leaves no run row at all, which is what AC-22 lets the owner
│                                                 rely on
├─ FileName               string(255)      high ← import_runs.file_name — the name the file came with, PRD §9
├─ AccountId              uuid?            high ← import_runs.account_id. Nullable twice over (decision 8): a
│                                                 HistoryMigration never had one, and ON DELETE SET NULL means a
│                                                 Statement run can lose one. Read it together with Kind
├─ RecordedRowCount       int(>=0)         high ← import_runs.recorded_row_count (AC-13). A stored column, not a
│                                                 count taken at read time: undo deletes the movement links while
│                                                 the run row survives, so a counted value would silently become 0
│                                                 (decision 6)
├─ AlreadyPresentRowCount int(>=0)         high ← import_runs.already_present_row_count (AC-13, AC-20, AC-21).
│                                                 Also stored — a row judged already there leaves no trace in the
│                                                 ledger to count
├─ CreatedAt              date-time        high ← import_runs.created_at — the day the file was handed over, PRD
│                                                 §9
└─ SetAside[]             SetAsideRow[]    high ← import_set_aside_rows, in file order. Carried in full here:
                                                  CLAUDE.md §API — a batch that finished is a success that reports
                                                  every item it skipped
   ├─ RowNumber           int(>=1)         high ← import_set_aside_rows.row_number — the row's 1-based ordinal in
   │                                              the file
   ├─ Reason              enum(3)          high ← import_set_aside_rows.reason VARCHAR(40) — NoRuleCovers (AC-08),
   │                                              TransferBetweenOwnAccounts (AC-06), ForeignCurrency (AC-07).
   │                                              Three, not four (decision 9): an unknown account refuses the
   │                                              whole load instead (AC-09)
   ├─ SourceCategory      string(200)?     high ← import_set_aside_rows.source_category. NULL when the file named
   │                                              no category for the row. AC-08 reads it to name the uncovered
   │                                              category back
   └─ RawLine             string(2000)     high ← import_set_aside_rows.raw_line (AC-13, AC-14). Raw bank text —
                                                  shop names the owner did not write. Confidential (sad.md §2),
                                                  never interpreted, never written to the logs (sad.md §7, §8)
```

### `migrateHistory` — `POST /api/v1/import-runs/history-migration`

```text
request  MigrateHistoryRequest                             (multipart/form-data)
└─ File                   binary           med  ← the export (ADR-0001). No account field: an export names an
                                                  account per row in the owner's own words and creates the ones
                                                  the ledger lacks (AC-10) — the opposite of a statement load,
                                                  which creates nothing (AC-09)

response 200  MigrateHistoryResponse                       (schema ImportRunResult)
└─ ... 9 fields                            high ← identical to loadStatement above, with AccountId always null
```

### `getImportRun` — `GET /api/v1/import-runs/{import_run_id}`

```text
path
└─ ImportRunId            uuid             high ← import_runs.id

query
├─ After                  string(200)?     med  ← opaque cursor over this run's set-aside rows (rules §3). The
│                                                 server mints it; the client passes it back unread and never
│                                                 builds one
├─ Before                 string(200)?     med  ← the same, backwards. Present because `before` is unusable
│                                                 without `prev_cursor`
└─ Limit                  int(1..200)      med  ← default 50. A size budget, not a latency one — PRD §6 carries no
                                                  per-page number. RawLine is capped at 2000 characters, so a
                                                  default page is at most ~100 KB. The numbers match core-ledger's
                                                  history paging

response 200  GetImportRunResponse                         (schema ImportRunReport)
├─ ... 8 run fields                        high ← identical to loadStatement above, minus SetAside
└─ SetAside               SetAsideRowPage  high ← the same rows, a page at a time
   ├─ Items[]             SetAsideRow[]    high ← see loadStatement. Ordered by RowNumber — the column data-
   │                                              model.md names for it, so the schema was ready for this decision
   │                                              either way
   ├─ HasNext             bool             med  ← page wrapper (rules §3)
   ├─ HasPrev             bool             med  ← page wrapper (rules §3)
   ├─ NextCursor          string(200)?     med  ← pass back as `after` to read the next page. null on the last
   │                                              page
   └─ PrevCursor          string(200)?     med  ← pass back as `before` to read the previous page. null on the
                                                  first page
```

### `undoImportRun` — `POST /api/v1/import-runs/{import_run_id}/undo`

```text
path
└─ ImportRunId            uuid             high ← import_runs.id

request  none
└─ —                                       med  ← the run id is the whole request. No Idempotency-Key: sad.md §6
                                                  shows no async actor anywhere in this feature, and a second undo
                                                  of the same run is refused with Import.AlreadyUndone rather
                                                  than silently repeated

response 200  UndoImportRunResponse                        (schema ImportRunReport)
└─ ... as getImportRun                     high ← Status flips to Undone. The counts keep their stored values, so
                                                  an undone run still reports what the load had done (decision 6).
                                                  The run row survives on purpose — it is the only trace in the
                                                  product that a load happened and was reversed, since core-ledger
                                                  keeps no audit trail (its ADR-0003)
```

### Error envelope, and what rides in `details`

```text
Error                                                      (docs/adr/0002 — flat, NOT Problem Details)
├─ Code                   string           high ← ^[A-Z][A-Za-z0-9]*\.[A-Z][A-Za-z0-9]*$ — the only part a client
│                                                 branches on. PascalCase, docs/adr/0003
├─ Message                string           high ← PRD §10 wording, never invented here
└─ Details                object?          med  ← optional structured context, per code — the table below
```

## Section B — drift findings (6-point checklist)

### 1. Operation ↔ data model *(core)* — ✓

Every leaf in the Section A trees maps to a column, with the type and nullability that column has.
No leaf disagrees with its column. Three groups are not columns, and each has a named origin rather
than a missing one:

- `FileInspectionResponse.SourceCategories[]` — read from the file, never stored on its own. PRD
  AC-01 asks for it; the bound is copied from the column that stores a category once it has a rule.
- `getImportRun.After` / `.Before` / `.Limit` — paging, a convention (rules §3), not state.
- `SetAsideRowPage.HasNext` / `HasPrev` / `NextCursor` / `PrevCursor` — the page wrapper.

Nullability is copied, not guessed: `AccountId`, `MappingProfileId`, `SourceCategory`,
`TargetCategoryId` and both cursors are 3.1 unions, `type: [string, "null"]`. No `nullable: true`
anywhere.

### 2. Error code ↔ definition in the repo *(core)* — ✓

**Checked against `src/` on run 5.** All 13 codes exist in the code, with the same strings. They
live where they are raised, as `core-ledger` does it: a Domain rule's code in its entity
(`MappingProfile`, `MappingRule`, `ImportRun`), a use case's code in
`src/FinNavis.Application/Import/ImportErrors.cs`. `src/FinNavis.Presentation/Errors/ErrorStatusCodes.cs`
maps each one to the status below. `CsvImportErrorCodeDriftTests` fails if a code is in `src/` and
not in this contract, or the other way round, or if a status differs. Each code appears exactly once
in the contract, and none collides with `core-ledger`'s — the modules `Import` and `MappingProfile`
are new.

| code | status | operation(s) | source |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Import.MissingRequiredColumn` | `400` | `inspectFile`, `loadStatement`, `migrateHistory` | PRD AC-03 · §6 flow 1 and flow 4, first alt-branch |
| `Import.FileNotReadable` | `400` | `inspectFile`, `loadStatement`, `migrateHistory` | PRD §6.1 abuse case · `sad.md` §8 Validation · bounds from `data-model.md` decision 10 |
| `Import.InvalidPaging` | `400` | `getImportRun` | the `limit` bound declared here; cursor is server-minted. **Removed from `undoImportRun` on run 5** — that operation takes no paging parameters |
| `Account.NotFound` | `404` | `loadStatement` | PRD AC-09 · §6 flow 2, first alt-branch · FK `import_runs.account_id` |
| `Import.NotFound` | `404` | `getImportRun`, `undoImportRun` | `import_runs.id` existence |
| `Import.MappingProfileNotConfirmed` | `409` | `loadStatement` | §6 flow 2, first alt-branch ("no rules exist for this shape") |
| `Import.AlreadyUndone` | `409` | `undoImportRun` | §6 flow 6, first alt-branch |
| `Import.MovementsChangedByHand` | `409` | `undoImportRun` | PRD AC-18 · §6 flow 6, second alt-branch · ADR-0008 |
| `Import.NotRecorded` | `500` | `loadStatement`, `migrateHistory` | PRD AC-22 · §6 flow 2, the failing-commit branch |
| `Category.NotFound` | `404` | `confirmMappingProfile` | PRD AC-02 · §6 flow 1, second alt-branch · FK `mapping_profile_rules.target_category_id` |
| `MappingProfile.InvalidRule` | `400` | `confirmMappingProfile` | `data-model.md` decision 12 — the `target` / `target_category_id` pairing, a domain invariant. `details` carries `{source_category, target}` (since run 5) |
| `MappingProfile.ShapeKeyInvalid` | `400` | `confirmMappingProfile` | `mapping_profiles.shape_key VARCHAR(1000)` — empty or longer. Added by hand 2026-10-31; **first listed here on run 5** |
| `MappingProfile.DuplicateSourceCategory` | `409` | `confirmMappingProfile` | UNIQUE (`mapping_profile_id`, `source_category`) |

**Module naming.** `Import` for the run and the load, `MappingProfile` for the profile, `Account`
and `Category` for the two `core-ledger` aggregates a load can fail to find. Every one is the
aggregate in the singular, PascalCase, and all satisfy the envelope's
`^[A-Z][A-Za-z0-9]*\.[A-Z][A-Za-z0-9]*$`.

**In a `*.NotFound` code the module is the aggregate that was not found** — `docs/adr/0004`,
Accepted 2026-10-30. That is why the three `404`s above carry `Account.NotFound`, `Category.NotFound`
and `Import.NotFound` rather than a module naming the operation that refused.

**Re-spelled 2026-10-22 by `docs/adr/0003`**, which replaced the snake_case baseline with
PascalCase across the repository — `import.account_not_found` became `Import.AccountNotFound`. All
12 codes changed case; none changed meaning, status or operation, so every row above holds as
written. The registry to build at `implement-tasks` follows the same split: class for the module,
member for the name, so `MappingProfileErrors.InvalidRule` returns
`"MappingProfile.InvalidRule"`.

**Verified on run 3, code by code.** Each of the 12 above matches ADR-0003's own mapping table;
the `Error.code` pattern in the contract is `^[A-Z][A-Za-z0-9]*\.[A-Z][A-Za-z0-9]*$`; the `Error`
schema description cites ADR-0003 and says the code is the one PascalCase value in a snake_case
body. No snake_case code survives anywhere in `openapi.yaml`. `core-ledger`'s 28 were re-spelled in
the same commit and carry the same pattern, so the repository holds one convention rather than two.

**ADR-0003 surfaced one finding, and run 3 said it did not touch this feature.** It did. The pair
`Category.GroupNotFound` / `CategoryGroup.NotFound` was `core-ledger`'s to merge, but the question
underneath it — what the module of a `*.NotFound` code names — reached both features, and
`core-ledger` run 3 parked it for exactly that reason. `docs/adr/0004` closed it on run 4 and this
contract moved in the same change.

Checked on run 4: no csv-import code duplicates another csv-import code. Two of them are now
**deliberately** the same string `core-ledger` returns — `Account.NotFound` and `Category.NotFound`
— which is one refusal under one code, not a collision.

**`application/problem+json` is off** (closed on run 5). `core-ledger` T24 routes every failure
through the one envelope, and `ErrorEnvelopeTests` and `CsvImportErrorEnvelopeTests` assert it for
routing 404s, binding failures and `Results.ValidationProblem`. A failure that stops a request
before any use case runs answers one of six pipeline codes (`Route.NotFound`, `Request.*`,
`Server.Unexpected`). They are in no feature contract **on purpose** — `docs/adr/0005` — so they are
not missing from the table above.

| `MappingRuleTarget enum [Category, TransferBetweenOwnAccounts]` | `mapping_profile_rules.target VARCHAR(30)`, decision 1 — two values | ✓ |
| `SetAsideReason enum` of three | `import_set_aside_rows.reason VARCHAR(40)`, decision 9 — three values | ✓ |
| `ImportRunKind enum [Statement, HistoryMigration]` | `import_runs.kind VARCHAR(20)` | ✓ |
| `ImportRunStatus enum [Completed, Undone]` | `import_runs.status VARCHAR(20)` — no `Failed` | ✓ |
| `row_number minimum: 1` | `import_set_aside_rows.row_number INTEGER NOT NULL`, 1-based | ✓ |
| counts `minimum: 0` | both `INTEGER NOT NULL` | ✓ |
| `target_category_id: [string, "null"]` | `mapping_profile_rules.target_category_id UUID NULL` | ✓ |
| `account_id: [string, "null"]` | `import_runs.account_id UUID NULL` | ✓ |

No bound is looser than its column, so the database cannot reject what the contract accepts. The
enums are string values, never ints (`CLAUDE.md`).

**The one bound deliberately absent** is a size limit on the uploaded file. **PRD §8 answered it on
2026-11-07: no limit is enforced** — a month's statement and six years of history are both a few
tens of kilobytes, and the installation stays off public networks. So the contract stays without a
`maxLength`, now as a decision rather than a gap. The code can still express a ceiling
(`CsvStatementReaderOptions.RowCeiling`, unset), and `Import.FileNotReadable` carries the refusal if
one is ever set.

### 5. OpenAPI ↔ sequence *(supporting)* — ✓ (deferred: six responses have no §6 branch)

**Every `alt`-branch in the six flows has a response.** Walked branch by branch:

| flow | branch | response |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | no date or no amount | `400 Import.MissingRequiredColumn` |
| 1 | the file can be read | `200 FileInspectionResponse` |
| 1 | a rule points at an unknown category | `404 Category.NotFound` |
| 1 | every rule points at something real | `201` / `200 MappingProfileResponse` |
| 2 | account missing **or** no rules for this shape | `404 Account.NotFound` / `409 Import.MappingProfileNotConfirmed` |
| 2 | row-level: transfer rule · no rule · foreign currency · already there · new | `SetAsideReason` ×3 · `AlreadyPresentRowCount` · `RecordedRowCount` |
| 2 | the commit fails | `500 Import.NotRecorded` |
| 2 | the commit succeeds | `200 LoadStatementResponse` |
| 3 | exact tier · proximity tier · nothing matches | `AlreadyPresentRowCount` · `AlreadyPresentRowCount` · `RecordedRowCount` |
| 4 | the export names no date, amount or account | `400 Import.MissingRequiredColumn` (export wording) |
| 4 | row-level: already there · transfer · transaction | the same three counters |
| 5 | one read of one run | `200 GetImportRunResponse` |
| 6 | the run was already undone | `409 Import.AlreadyUndone` |
| 6 | a movement no longer matches its fingerprint | `409 Import.MovementsChangedByHand` |
| 6 | every movement is as the load wrote it | `200 UndoImportRunResponse` with `Status: Undone` |

**Responses with no §6 branch (sequence gaps) — six, all legitimate.** A sequence diagram draws
state and ordering refusals; it does not draw request-shape checks, uniqueness or existence:

1. `Import.FileNotReadable` — PRD §6.1 abuse case, enforced while the file streams (ADR-0006).
2. `Import.InvalidPaging` — paging shape, introduced by this contract.
3. `MappingProfile.InvalidRule` — the `target` / `target_category_id` pairing, `data-model.md`
   decision 12.
4. `MappingProfile.DuplicateSourceCategory` — a UNIQUE index.
5. `Import.NotFound` — flows 5 and 6 assume the run exists.
6. `MappingProfile.ShapeKeyInvalid` — the `shape_key` bound. **Added on run 5**: the code arrived
   by hand on 2026-10-31, after run 4.

**No flow maps to no operation**, and no operation lacks a flow.

### 6. Contract ↔ the served document *(supporting, FinNavis)* — ✓

**Checked on run 5 (epic task T27).** Runs 1–4 marked this N/A, because `Endpoints/` held only a
`.gitkeep`. Now the API was started in Development and `/openapi/v1.json` was diffed against this
file by a script that resolves every `$ref` on both sides and compares, per operation: the
`operationId`, the parameters, the request body per content type, every status, and every field of
every request and response schema with its type, format and required flag.

**Matches:** all six paths and methods, all six `operationId`s, every status code, every field
name, and every enum value (1:1). The endpoint-folder tree below is the one on disk. Every refusal
answers the flat envelope; none answers `application/problem+json` (drift point 2).

**Fixed on this run** (see "What changed on run 5"): `InvalidRule` details in the code, strict
numbers in the code, and the unreachable `400` on `undoImportRun` in the contract.

**Accepted as generator artifacts** — by the owner on 2026-11-08. The served document differs, but
what crosses the wire matches the contract, so the code was not bent to change the markup:

| served document says | the contract says | why the wire already matches |
|---|---|---|
| enum schemas with no `type: string` | `type: string` + `enum` | the values are identical, and `JsonStringEnumConverter` refuses an integer |
| `details: [null, object]` | `details: object`, optional | the envelope never writes a null `details` (`JsonIgnoreCondition.WhenWritingNull`) |
| multipart `file` and `account_id` not `required` | both `required` | binding still refuses a request that leaves one out; the generator does not mark form parts |
| integers carry `format: int32` | no `format` | extra precision in the markup only; every count is far below `int32` |

**One behaviour the served document cannot show, found by the quality gates (T25).** The contract
says, for AC-11, that a history row naming two accounts becomes a transfer. No load records a
transfer today: the import pipeline only records transactions. Neither document can show this,
because it is behaviour behind an unchanged `200`. It is a code gap, not contract drift, and is
listed in Section D so it is not lost.

**The folder tree this contract commits to** — six folders, matching `sad.md` §5 exactly, none
added and none dropped. **Confirmed on disk on run 5:**

```text
src/FinNavis.Presentation/Endpoints/
├── MappingProfiles/
│   ├── Inspect/        inspectFile              POST /api/v1/mapping-profiles/inspect
│   └── Confirm/        confirmMappingProfile    POST /api/v1/mapping-profiles
└── ImportRuns/
    ├── LoadStatement/  loadStatement            POST /api/v1/import-runs/statement
    ├── MigrateHistory/ migrateHistory           POST /api/v1/import-runs/history-migration
    ├── Get/            getImportRun             GET  /api/v1/import-runs/{import_run_id}
    └── Undo/           undoImportRun            POST /api/v1/import-runs/{import_run_id}/undo
```

- **`application/problem+json` was still on** — closed by `core-ledger` T24; asserted by

- **Drift point 6 was unchecked** — closed by epic task T27 (this run).
- **No size limit on an uploaded file** — closed upstream: PRD §8 answered on 2026-11-07, no limit

- **`SKILL.md` still stated the snake_case spelling** — closed upstream: both lines now say

| what | why parked | next step |

| Six responses with no §6 `alt`-branch | All six are shape, uniqueness or existence checks, which a sequence diagram legitimately omits | None required. Re-check at `--reconcile` if §6 ever grows a validation branch |

The same goes for the message for "both `after` and `before` given", which reuses the unknown-cursor sentence and does not fit | Add the rows to PRD §10 (and a separate sentence for both cursors), then copy them into the examples here and into `ImportErrors` word for word |

The contract is right; the code is behind it. Neither `/openapi/v1.json` nor this file can show the gap, because the response stays an unchanged `200` | Decide whether the old tracker's export names transfers (PRD §8, settled by T01), then extend the pipeline and `MigrateHistory`, with a quality-gate test |

**Accepted as is (no action, reason recorded):**

- **AC-02's message says "with that name" while a rule points at a category by id.** PRD §10's
  wording is kept **verbatim**, because that is the sentence the owner reads; the id and the
  file's own category text go into `details`. Changing the PRD to say "id" would make the message
  worse for the person reading it.
- **A finished load answers `200`, not `201`, even though it creates an import run.** Fixed by
  `CLAUDE.md` §API and `.claude/rules/openapi.md` §6 — a batch that finished is a `200` with
  counts and per-item reasons. No `Location` header is sent; `ImportRunId` is in the body.
  Flagged here because it is the one place this contract looks unusual next to `core-ledger`,
  which answers `201` for every create.
- **`SetAsideRow` carries no id**, although `import_set_aside_rows.id` exists. Nothing addresses a
  set-aside row: AC-14 says it is never recorded on its own, and only a later load of the same
  file can record it. `RowNumber` is what locates the line in the file.
- **No money field anywhere.** A load reports counts and raw lines; balances follow from the
  movements (`core-ledger` ADR-0002). Recorded there so the next reader does not think the
  money-as-a-string rule was forgotten.
- **Four markup differences in `/openapi/v1.json`** — enums without `type`, a nullable `details`,
  multipart parts not marked `required`, `format: int32`. Accepted by the owner on 2026-11-08 as
  generator artifacts; drift point 6 says why the wire still matches.
- **Six pipeline codes are in no feature contract** — `Route.NotFound`, `Request.MethodNotAllowed`,
  `Request.UnsupportedMediaType`, `Request.Invalid`, `Request.ValidationFailed`,
  `Server.Unexpected`. They stop a request before any use case runs and are the same for every
  feature, so they are defined once in Presentation. `docs/adr/0005`, Accepted 2026-11-08.
- **`confirmMappingProfile` answers `200` when a shape is re-confirmed.** `data-model.md`
  (`mapping_profile_rules`) says re-confirming replaces the rules wholesale, and AC-04 says that
  changes nothing already recorded. Two success codes on one operation is the honest shape.

## Decisions settled at this gate

Six were settled in run 1. **Runs 2 and 3 settled none** — no upstream document asked a new
question, and re-opening a settled one would overwrite a reviewed design. `docs/adr/0003` did
answer a question that first came up at this gate, but it answered it as an ADR, which is where a
repo-wide convention belongs; this report only verifies the result. The six below are repeated
because the chat they were agreed in is gone at the next `/clear`.

1. **Does the confirm step carry the same file again?** Source: `sad.md` §6, "Left for the
   API-contract stage".
   → **No. It carries the `shape_key` that `inspectFile` returned.** Chosen by the owner. ADR-0001
   keeps nothing between the two calls, and the shape key is the readable normalised header row
   (`data-model.md` decision 2), not an upload id — so passing it back costs nothing and keeps the
   total at two uploads per new bank, which is exactly what ADR-0001 priced. The residual risk is
   a profile stored against a shape no real file has; it is harmless, because a shape key no file
   matches simply never matches.

2. **Is a run's set-aside list paged, and how is it ordered?** Source: `sad.md` §6 "Left for the
   API-contract stage" and `data-model.md` Open items.
   → **In full on the load, paged by opaque cursor on the read, ordered by `row_number`.** Chosen
   by the owner. The load answers in full because `CLAUDE.md` §API fixes that shape for a batch
   that finished. The read pages it because a history migration is ~1500 rows (PRD §6) and each
   set-aside row carries up to 2000 characters of raw bank text, so a report read on every visit
   would carry that weight every time. `row_number` is the column `data-model.md` already names
   for the ordering.

3. **What are the field names of the batch report?** Source: `sad.md` §6, "the field names are not
   set anywhere yet".
   → **`recorded_row_count`, `already_present_row_count`, `set_aside[]`**, each with
   `{row_number, reason, source_category, raw_line}`. The two counts take their names from the
   columns that store them, so contract and schema cannot drift apart on the wording.

4. **What status refuses a load whose shape has no confirmed rules?** Source: `sad.md` §6 flow 2,
   first alt-branch; no PRD row.
   → **`409`, not `404`.** The request is well-formed and the client named no profile — the server
   derived the shape from the file. The world refuses the load because of its state, and the
   client's next move is inspect-then-confirm, not "fix the id you sent".

5. **What is the page size for set-aside rows?** Source: this contract.
   → **min 1, max 200, default 50**, justified by a **size** budget and said so plainly: PRD §6
   carries no per-page latency number, only ≤ 60 s for a whole load and ≤ 30 s for a whole undo.
   `raw_line` is bounded at 2000 characters, so a default page is at most ~100 KB. The numbers
   match `core-ledger`'s history paging so a client uses one rule for both.

6. **Which tables stay off the API?** Source: drift point 4.
   → **The four link tables and the fingerprint.** They are undo bookkeeping (ADR-0007, ADR-0008),
   and AC-13 asks for counts and set-aside rows, never for the list of movements a run wrote.
   Recorded here so a later reader does not mistake the absence for an oversight.

**Run 5 settled four more, all from the served-document diff, all chosen by the owner:**

7. **Does the API accept a number sent as a string?** → **No.** `NumberHandling = Strict`; such a
   request is `400 Request.Invalid`. The contract types every count as a JSON number.
8. **What happens to the markup differences where the wire already matches?** → **Recorded, not
   fixed.** Four generator artifacts, listed in drift point 6. Changing the code only to change the
   markup of a document nobody consumes would add code with no behaviour behind it.
9. **Does `undoImportRun` page its set-aside rows?** → **No.** Its report is the first page; the
   client pages through `getImportRun`. So its `400 Import.InvalidPaging` was removed.
10. **Contract or code for `InvalidRule`'s `details`?** → **The contract.** The code now names the
    refused rule by `source_category` and `target`.

**Nothing re-decided.** Authentication, the error envelope, money on the wire, cursor paging, the
batch outcome, URL versioning, snake_case JSON keys, UUID v7 ids, UTC timestamps and string enums
were all read from `CLAUDE.md`, `.claude/rules/openapi.md` and the ADRs, and none was reopened on
any of the three runs. The one convention that **did** change — the case of an error code — changed
in `docs/adr/0003`, not here.

## What `--reconcile` will read first

1. **PRD §10** — whether rows for `Import.FileNotReadable` and `Import.InvalidPaging` landed. If
   they did, copy each sentence into the examples here word for word, and check every other
   `example.message` still equals its row.
2. **The AC-11 transfer gap** — once a load records transfers, re-check `migrateHistory`'s
   description and whether a new refusal appeared.
3. **`/openapi/v1.json`** — re-run the T27 diff whenever an endpoint changes. Only the four accepted
   artifacts in drift point 6 may remain; anything else is drift.
4. **`docs/adr/`** — whether another project-wide record landed, as `0003`, `0004` and `0005` did.
   A record that changes the shape of `code`, `message` or `details` reaches all 13 responses at
   once.
